stages.goal: Measure armchair tube geometry needed for the T layout
checks: measured C–C bond length and (8,8)/(4,4) radii from hand-built chiral vectors
axial repeat length measured for 8-unit main and 4-unit branch
bond-length spread small enough to define one seam tolerance

experiment.question: what C–C bond length, radius and axial repeat do hand-generated (8,8) and (4,4) armchair cells actually give?
experiment.method: generate minimal armchair unit cells from explicit chiral vectors (no prebuilt tube generator), measure bond lengths, radii, axial periods
experiment.stop_condition: stop after printing measured bond length, radii and axial repeats

stages.goal: Build and check a seamless sp2 T-junction from the measured geometry
checks: main (8,8) x8 with open ends; branch (4,4) x4 perpendicular to centre sidewall, open end
elliptical hole cut in main sidewall; one connected carbon seam (no dangling bonds or reported leftovers)
both lumens connected; three distal ends uncapped
non-periodic cell with >=8 A vacuum on every axis
coordinates generated by own Python; user ban on prebuilt nanotube generators respected

experiment.question: can a bounded set of hole sizes and local add/remove/reposition steps close the branch-to-main seam in one connected network?
experiment.method: bounded trial loop over branch cut position and hole-size offsets using probe radii, keeping best seam by dangling-bond count and bond-length spread
experiment.stop_condition: finite trials; report best seam metrics and any unmet constraint as unfinished

stages.goal: Export extxyz, write back to Atom Structure, read back
checks: extxyz saved in authorized Sandbox and re-parsed with matching atom count and coordinates
connected Atom Structure read back confirms same atom count and non-periodic box
short report states only the verified seam result
